reason: Checked independently. Re-aggregating recheck3_out.json (56 exp60 clips, official tools/official tracking_cellmot DistanceMatching at 7 um) gives exactly the numbers in the finding: FN 1,705 (miss 834, both_linked 555, one_free 305, both_free 11); for the both_linked cases the GT link is 3.17 um, the matched predicted nodes are 9.13 um apart (9.06 with flow), our links are 1.60/1.53 um and our matched nodes sit 3.91/4.20 um from the GT nuclei; 0 true 2x2 swaps. The 2x2 rule finds 51 raw / 57 flow candidates, destroys 0 TP and creates 1. A new measurement (scratchpad v_rc_a_extra.py) backs the detection-side reading. The nearest predicted node to GT nucleus a is 3.89 um away (median), the second nearest is 6.59 um, and the matched node is the nearest one in 90% of cases, so there is no closer unmatched detection a relink could use. Our own track's next node is a median 6.85 um from GT b (within 7 um in 52% of cases, and within 7 um at both ends in 41%), about 2.1 um farther than the node the matcher picks. So each GT nucleus sits between two distinct predicted tracks about 9 um apart (not duplicates) and the matcher switches between them. No linking or post-processing rule can fix that. 6bba holds 485 of the 555 cases, so this is dense-tissue localization. Feasibility is trivial: no build, nothing to gate, R1-R10 unaffected. One small correction: 'only detector retraining' overstates it slightly, since localization or coordinate-head retraining also counts, and all of these are after the deadline.
